newsitem.title: FRANCE: French hotel occupancy up one point at 61.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: French hotel occupancy up one point at 61.8 pct.

text.p: The occupancy rate at French hotel chains rose one percentage point last year to 61.8 percent, with the biggest rise of 5.5 percent registered in the one-star hotel segment, consultants MKG Conseil said on Thursday.

The average price of a room fell 1.4 percent to 356 francs from 361 francs in 1995, with the biggest drop seen in the four-star segment, where prices fell 4.6 percent, MKG said in a statement. The volume of available rooms in French hotel chains rose 2.7 percent to 210,585, with gains seen in all segments.
Turnover rose 2.3 percent, but revenue per available room slipped 0.4 percent to 216.60 francs in 1996, it said.
